title: Pokomo Fish Curry
author: Chef Amina Hassan

heritage.origin: Tana River County — Pokomo heartland along the Tana River
heritage.history: The Pokomo are a Bantu community inhabiting the Tana River Delta. They are an agricultural and fishing community — the Tana River provides freshwater fish central to the Pokomo diet. Pokomo fish curry uses freshwater fish prepared with curry spices influenced by coastal proximity while maintaining distinctly Pokomo characteristics.
heritage.modernEvolution: Pokomo cuisine is little-known outside the community — this dish represents an important record of a unique food culture.

desc: Pokomo Fish Curry — Tana River freshwater fish simmered in a fragrant tomato and onion curry sauce with mild coastal spices. The fish curry of the Pokomo people — shaped by river, forest, and coastal proximity.
longDesc: The Pokomo fish curry reflects a community at the intersection of inland river life and coastal influence. The Tana River provides the fish; the proximity to the coast introduces the curry spices.
ingredients: 600g freshwater fish fillets — tilapia or catfish
steps: Season fish with salt and turmeric.
Cook onions until golden. Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, curry powder, turmeric, and cumin. Cook for 6—8 minutes.
Add water. Bring to a simmer.
Add fish. Spoon sauce over gently.
Cover and simmer 8—12 minutes until fish is cooked.
chefTips: Freshwater fish has a slightly earthier flavour that works beautifully with the spice blend.
Catfish from the Tana River is the traditional choice.
commonMistakes: Too thin sauce before adding fish.
cookingScience: Freshwater fish generally have a higher fat content than lean saltwater fish, contributing to a richer, more satisfying curry.
sustainabilityTips: The Tana River Delta is an ecologically sensitive area — sustainable fishing practices are essential.
servedWith: Wild Greens from the Tana River area
culturalNote: The Pokomo represent one of Kenya's most distinctive communities — a river people whose entire culture is shaped by the Tana River and its delta.
